[USER] User expressed interest in anatomical adaptations of ospreys for catching fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys have sharp, curved talons for better grip on prey.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys have scaled soles covered with rough scales to grip wet surfaces like fish scales.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys possess powerful, muscular legs and feet for diving into water and lifting heavy fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys have a sharp, hooked beak for tearing apart the flesh of their prey.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys have long, narrow wings for soaring, gliding, and maneuverability while diving.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These adaptations make ospreys highly specialized and efficient fish-hunting birds.  
[USER] User expressed amazement at the adaptations of ospreys.  
[USER] User inquired about the diving speed of ospreys when catching fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys can dive into the water at speeds of up to 80 km/h (50 mph).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys can plunge from heights of up to 30 metres (100 feet) into the water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys close their wings, extend their legs forward, and dive beak-first into the water to catch fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys' powerful wings and aerodynamic body shape provide significant lift and maneuverability.

[USER] User asked if ospreys eat anything other than fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys primarily eat fish, catching about 99% of their prey from water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In rare cases, ospreys may prey on small mammals, reptiles, or birds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some ospreys have been observed feeding on small rodents, snakes, or birds, but these instances are rare.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Non-fish prey items make up a tiny proportion of an osprey’s diet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ospreys are highly adapted to feed on fish, with unique anatomical features aiding in this specialization.
